extracted.intended_audience: writers, editors, students, and other professionals who want to use inclusive/conscious language
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writers and editors on using conscious, inclusive, and respectful language across topics (ability, race, gender, age, images, children’s books, etc.), with best practices and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use language to include, respect, and empower
rubrics_metrics.description: To learn how you can use language to include, respect, and empower, explore the topics below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site positions itself as an essential guide to conscious language — offering news, observations, and guidance. The core evaluative principle is whether language choices include people, show respect, and empower those described; apply recommended phrasing and approaches from the guide and newsletter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider images as well as words (picture books and unconscious bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: For children’s books, a copyeditor looks at more than words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate artwork/photographs/illustrations for unconscious bias and representation in addition to the prose. Copyediting children's books should include scrutiny of images and how they reinforce or counter stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear 'why' in sensitivity reads to build trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Building trust with readers by providing a clear why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors request or act on sensitivity reads (especially when writing characters from groups other than their own), explain the purpose and rationale behind editorial choices so readers and communities understand intent and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasizing gender (courtesy titles, obituaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rethinking Courtesy Titles in Obituaries — It’s time to show respect by not overemphasizing gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer forms and conventions that do not highlight gender unnecessarily (for example, when choosing courtesy titles or phrasing in obituaries); favor respectful, non-gendered or minimally gendered options where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain Language (listed as a core topic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clarity, accessibility, and straightforward phrasing so writing is comprehensible to a broad audience. See the Plain Language topic for concrete tactics and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply topic-specific best practices (ability, age, race, gender, health, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse by Topic: Ability + Disability; Age; Appearance; Climate + Environment; Ethnicity, Race + Nationality; Gender, Sex + Sexuality; Health; Socioeconomic Status; Spirituality, Religion + Atheism; Miscellaneous; Creative Writing; Design + Images; Empowerment; Plain Language; Teaching Children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guide’s topic pages for tailored guidance and examples. Each topic contains specific recommended language, considerations, and anti-patterns relevant to that subject area; follow those targeted recommendations when writing or editing about those topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor practical examples and reproducible best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: For best practices and hundreds of everyday examples, get the new style guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing language choices, prefer guidance backed by concrete example phrasings and repeatable best-practice rules rather than vague admonitions; consult the full style guide or newsletter for many everyday instances and implementation details.
